plate_provenance.prompt: Cinematic photorealistic space-documentary still of the surface of Venus. In the lower two-thirds, slightly right of center, sits a heavy Soviet Venera-style planetary lander probe with a spherical titanium pressure hull, a wide scalloped serrated aerodynamic brake collar disk, cylindrical sensor housings, a top helical helical antenna mast, and a heavy circular shock-absorbing landing ring resting on jagged, fractured dark volcanic basalt slabs. The lander's lower metallic hull, landing ring, support struts, and edges are intensely incandescent, glowing bright cherry red-orange and crimson-gold from the crushing 465-degree Celsius furnace atmospheric heat, casting vibrant orange-red thermal illumination onto the cracked basalt rocks beneath. The scorching Venusian landscape features jagged basalt plates with faint glowing molten red-orange thermal fractures in the rock, leading toward a massive hazy volcanic shield volcano mountain on the horizon. The top twenty-two percent of the frame features a thick, dense, hazy dark-amber and sulfuric orange-yellow cloud deck across the sky. High contrast, saturated warm crimson, amber-gold, and furnace-orange color palette with deep warm shadows, 8k resolution, razor-sharp hardware and geological texture, authentic space probe engineering detail, absolutely no text, no numbers, no labels, no logos, no human figures, no robots.
